content: MTUS1, also known as Mitochondrial Tumor Suppressor 1 or Microtubule-Associated Scaffold Protein 1, is a protein encoded by the MTUS1 gene in humans. It is considered a candidate tumor suppressor protein. The expression levels of MTUS1 have been reported to be lost in various types of human malignancies, including cancers of the colon, ovary, head and neck, pancreas, breast, bladder, stomach, and lung. As a result of alternative splicing, the MTUS1 gene encodes five distinct protein isoforms, which are named ATIP1, ATIP2, ATIP3a, ATIP3b, and ATIP4. Among these, ATIP3a and ATIP3b are generally grouped together as ATIP3. The major splice variants encoded by the MTUS1 gene are ATIP1 and ATIP3. The protein encoded by this gene contains a C-terminal domain that interacts with the angiotensin II receptor type 2 (AT2) and a large coiled-coil region that facilitates dimerization. Multiple alternatively spliced transcript variants encoding different isoforms have been identified for this gene. One of these transcript variants encodes a mitochondrial protein that functions as a tumor suppressor and is involved in AT2 signaling pathways. Other transcript variants may encode nuclear or transmembrane proteins, but it remains unclear whether these variants also participate in AT2 signaling pathways. MTUS1 has been shown to interact with the angiotensin II receptor type 2.
